rules.message: runs-on label '{label}' is a GitHub-hosted runner label; Forgejo and Gitea runners only carry the labels they were registered with, and a label maps to whatever image the admin mapped it to. On Forgejo a job whose label no runner declares waits until such a runner appears; Gitea's runner falls back to its own default image, which is not GitHub's.
rules.fix_hint: Use a label your runner declares (often `docker` or `self-hosted`), or register a runner with this label and an image that provides the tools the job expects; do not assume GitHub's preinstalled software.

rules.message: `{uses}` uses the v4 artifact API; the Forgejo documentation requires v3 (or the patched v4 fork) for the upload and download artifact actions.
rules.fix_hint: Pin `actions/upload-artifact@v3` / `actions/download-artifact@v3`, use the patched v4 fork linked from the Forgejo artifacts documentation, or publish the files another way (package registry, release asset).

rules.message: `{uses}` analyses code and uploads the results to GitHub code scanning. Forgejo has no security-report storage and Gitea does not support the `security-events` token scope, so the upload has nowhere to go.
rules.fix_hint: Drop the step, or run an analyser that writes a report you keep as a job artifact (SARIF can be stored as a file even where no forge consumes it).

rules.message: `{uses}` signs a build with a GitHub OIDC token and uploads the result to the GitHub attestations API; neither the token nor that API exists on Forgejo or Gitea.
rules.fix_hint: Sign and publish provenance yourself (for example cosign with a key stored as a secret) and attach it as an artifact or release asset, or drop the step.

rules.message: `{uses}` publishes to GitHub Pages. Forgejo has no built-in Pages service and Gitea does not support the `pages` token scope, so the deployment cannot happen.
rules.fix_hint: Publish the site another way: push the built files to a pages branch served by your forge's static hosting, or deploy to an external host over SSH/rsync with a secret.

rules.message: `permissions: id-token: write` asks GitHub for an OIDC token. Forgejo ignores the job `permissions` key and spells this `enable-openid-connect: true` instead; Gitea does not support the `id-token` scope at all, so any step exchanging the token for cloud credentials fails.
rules.fix_hint: On Forgejo set `enable-openid-connect: true` on the job and re-check the issuer and audience your cloud provider trusts; on Gitea replace the OIDC login with a long-lived credential stored as a secret.

rules.message: job-level `environment:` is listed as unsupported workflow syntax and ignored by Gitea Actions: there are no deployment environments, so environment secrets, variables, protection rules and approvals do not apply.
rules.fix_hint: Move the environment's secrets and variables to repository or organisation level and gate the job with an `if:` condition; do not rely on the environment for manual approval.

rules.message: `on.pull_request.types` contains {types}. Forgejo and Gitea derive these types from their own `label_updated` and `label_cleared` events: for pull requests `label_updated` is reported as `labeled` whether a label was added or removed, and `unlabeled` only arrives when the labels are cleared.
rules.fix_hint: Do not use the event type to tell adding from removing: trigger on `labeled` and compare the labels in the payload (or the API) inside the job.

rules.message: the job runs in a `container:` and uses the JavaScript action `{uses}`; the runner executes JavaScript actions with the node binary inside that image, so an image without node breaks the step.
rules.fix_hint: Use an image that ships node, add node to your image, or replace the action with a `run:` step.

rules.message: the step reaches GitHub through {what}. Inside a Forgejo or Gitea job, `GITHUB_API_URL` and `github.api_url` point at the forge's own Gitea-compatible REST API, the job token is not a github.com token, and Gitea leaves `GITHUB_GRAPHQL_URL` empty because it has no GraphQL API (which the gh CLI relies on).
rules.fix_hint: Call the forge API at `${{ github.api_url }}` (`$GITHUB_API_URL`) with the job token, or replace the gh CLI with `tea` or plain `curl`; keep the hard-coded api.github.com call only where you really mean github.com and pass a github.com token.

rules.message: portability unknown: `{action}` is not covered by a rule, so nothing about it has been checked. The forge resolves a bare `uses:` against its configured actions host, and what the action does at runtime (GitHub API calls, GitHub-only tooling) is invisible to a static check.
rules.fix_hint: Make sure the action is reachable from your instance (an absolute `uses:` URL works where the default host is not), and read it for github.com API calls before relying on it.
